Reads jobs from CleanerCrm.Scheduling (exists on disk) — read-only; do NOT modify scheduling*, schedule_live/*, client_live/*, quoting*, audit* (other agents own them).

Verify: mix compile clean, mix format, MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.migrate, `mix spex test/spex/837_send_automated_appointment_reminders_to_clients/`, `mix test` no regressions.

Final response: files, 837 pass/fail, blockers. Under 150 words.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- codemyspec:design: Architecture design, UI design system, and technology strategy. Use before writing code to plan how to build it.
- codemyspec:develop: Full-lifecycle development — context orchestration, LiveView orchestration, and interactive refactoring. Spawns subagents for multi-step workflows.
- codemyspec:implement: Autonomous implementation loop — start or stop requirements-driven development. The agent walks the requirement graph automatically.
- codemyspec:init: Project setup, authentication, and sync. Use when starting a new project, logging in, or refreshing stale state.
- codemyspec:next: Find and start the next requirement task in one gesture. Use after each completed task as your single onboarding instruction.
- codemyspec:product: Product management — guided story interview, review, and Three Amigos sessions. Use when defining what to build, refining requirements, reviewing story quality, or running an Example Mapping session on a story.
- codemyspec:qa: QA testing and issue management — full app QA, per-story QA, integration planning, issue triage, and fixes.
- codemyspec:sync: Sync project components and regenerate architecture views. Use after git pulls, before design sessions, or when views feel stale.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

defmodule CleanerCrm.MixProject do
  use Mix.Project

  def project do
    [
      app: :cleaner_crm,
      version: "0.1.0",
      elixir: "~> 1.19",
      elixirc_paths: elixirc_paths(Mix.env()),
      start_permanent: Mix.env() == :prod,
      aliases: aliases(),
      deps: deps(),
      compilers: compilers(Mix.env()),
      listeners: [Phoenix.CodeReloader]
    ]
  end

  # Configuration for the OTP application.
  #
  # Type `mix help compile.app` for more information.
  def application do
    [
      mod: {CleanerCrmWeb.Application, []},
      extra_applications: [:logger, :runtime_tools]
    ]
  end

  def cli do
    [
      preferred_envs: [precommit: :test, spex: :test]
    ]
  end

  defp compilers(:test),
    do: [:diagnostics, :boundary, :phoenix_live_view, :erlang, :elixir, :spex, :app]

  defp compilers(_),
    do: [:diagnostics, :boundary, :phoenix_live_view, :erlang, :elixir, :app]

  # Specifies which paths to compile per environment.
  defp elixirc_paths(:test), do: ["lib", "test/support"]
  defp elixirc_paths(_), do: ["lib"]

  # Specifies your project dependencies.
  #
  # Type `mix help deps` for examples and options.
  defp deps do
    [
      {:bcrypt_elixir, "~> 3.0"},
      {:phoenix, "~> 1.8.8"},
      {:phoenix_ecto, "~> 4.5"},
      {:ecto_sql, "~> 3.13"},
      {:postgrex, ">= 0.0.0"},
      {:phoenix_html, "~> 4.1"},
      {:phoenix_live_reload, "~> 1.2", only: :dev},
      {:phoenix_live_view, "~> 1.2.0"},
      {:lazy_html, ">= 0.1.0", only: :test},

      end

        client =
          Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{

            email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
            preferred_channel: :sms

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Curated bridge from BDD specs into in-app state.

  The only module that may dep on `CleanerCrm` from inside the spex test
  tree. Declared as its own top-level Boundary so the spec boundary
  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.

  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
  """

  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]

  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
            [
              CleanerCrm.Clients,
              CleanerCrm.Scheduling,
              CleanerCrm.Quality,
              CleanerCrm.Billing,
              CleanerCrm.TimeTracking,
              CleanerCrm.Notifications
            ]}

  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
    user
  end

  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
  #
  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false
        })
      )

    client
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled
        })
      )

    job
  end

  def job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })
      )

    invoice
  end

  # Time tracking (story 838) — a resolved clock-in/out record for a
  # job.
  #
  # Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  # 838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job). Scenarios whose subject is a downstream pay
  # calculation (hourly vs. piece-rate, running pay-period totals,
  # payroll CSV export) seed the resolved time entry directly here
  # instead of re-driving the clock-in/out flow every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, time_entry} =
      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })
      )

    time_entry
  end

  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder
  # with its confirm/reschedule token.
  #
  # The automatic "reminder sent at the configured lead time" trigger
  # is covered end-to-end by story 837's own "reminder fires at the
  # configured lead time" spec. Scenarios whose subject is a
  # downstream decision on an existing reminder (confirm, reschedule,
  # delivery-status fallback) seed the already-sent notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the scheduler trigger every
  # time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def notification_fixture(scope, client, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :reminder,
          channel: :email,
          status: :sent,
          token: "reminder_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change
  # notification already pushed to a cleaner.
  #
  # The push itself (a moved or cancelled job creating this
  # notification) is covered end-to-end by story 843's own "moved job
  # notifies the cleaner" / "cancelled job notifies the cleaner"
  # specs, which drive the real trigger via `ScheduleLive.Board`.
  # Scenarios whose subject is a downstream decision on an existing
  # pending change (acknowledging, re-prompting, office visibility,
  # escalation, channel fallback) seed the already-pushed notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the board move every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md. Never pass
  # `status: :acknowledged` here — the acknowledgment round-trip
  # through `FieldLive.Today` is the whole point of story 843.
  def schedule_change_notification_fixture(scope, cleaner, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :schedule_change,
          channel: :push,
          status: :pending,
          change_summary: "Job schedule changed",
          pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          token: "schedule_change_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Quality (story 839) — a job carrying an unfinished, per-job
  # checklist of required and optional tasks.
  #
  # Checking items off and completing the job through the checklist UI
  # is the subject under test in `FieldLive.Job`, so this fixture stops
  # short of that — it only seeds the checklist itself. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md: `ChecklistTemplate` assignment
  # (story 842) has its own creation flow this fixture skips.
  def job_with_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
        %{task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true},
        %{task: "Fridge interior wiped down", required: false}
      ])

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Quality (story 842) — a job carrying an unfinished, room-grouped
  # checklist whose items are exactly what the caller passes in.
  #
  # Story 842 owns the `ChecklistTemplate` -> per-job `Checklist`
  # assignment flow (which room/task combinations count as in scope for
  # a given job). That assignment UI doesn't exist yet and isn't part
  # of this story's component list (only `FieldLive.ChecklistComponent`
  # is), so seeding the already-instantiated, room-tagged checklist
  # directly is the sanctioned bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — the
  # subject under test is opening/working the checklist on
  # `FieldLive.Job`, not how it got assigned. `items` is a list of
  # `%{room:, task:, required:}` maps; a spec proving an out-of-scope
  # task never appears simply omits it from `items`.
  def job_with_room_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, items, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} = CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, items)

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end
end

2	  @moduledoc """
3	  A paying customer with contact info and preferences.
4	
5	  Scoped to an account: every client belongs to exactly one account and
6	  is only ever visible within that account.
7	  """
8

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients.Client do
  @moduledoc """
  A paying customer with contact info and preferences.

  Scoped to an account: every client belongs to exactly one account and
  is only ever visible within that account.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t() | nil,
          active: boolean(),
          card_on_file: boolean(),
          properties: [CleanerCrm.Clients.Property.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "clients" do
    field :name, :string
    field :active, :boolean, default: true
    field :card_on_file, :boolean, default: false

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    has_many :properties, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(client, attrs) do
    client
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :active, :card_on_file])
    |> validate_required([:name], message: "is required")
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 200)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients do
  @moduledoc """
  Clients and their properties: addresses, parking notes, entry
  methods and codes, pets, and cleaning preferences — the authoritative
  access and scope record every job carries.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.{Client, Property}
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder

  ## Clients

  def list_clients(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([c], asc: c.name)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_client!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Client{account_id: account_id}
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def change_client(%Scope{}, %Client{} = client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Client.changeset(client, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Lists only active clients, for the account's day-to-day client list.
  """
  def list_active_clients(%Scope{} = scope) do
    scope |> list_clients() |> Enum.filter(& &1.active)
  end

  def update_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{} = client, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    client
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  def deactivate_client(%Scope{} = scope, %Client{} = client) do
    update_client(scope, client, %{"active" => false})
  end

  def reactivate_client(%Scope{} = scope, %Client{} = client) do
    update_client(scope, client, %{"active" => true})
  end

  @doc """
  Permanently deletes a client and its properties.

  Refuses to delete a client that still has dependent records (e.g.
  scheduled jobs) elsewhere in the system — the database's foreign key
  constraints are the source of truth for what's "dependent," so this
  context stays ignorant of any other bounded context's schema.
  """
  def delete_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{} = client)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.delete(client)
  rescue
    Ecto.ConstraintError -> {:error, :has_upcoming_jobs}
  end

  ## Properties

  @doc """
  Lists a client's properties, ordered by address.
  """
  def list_properties(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{id: client_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id and p.client_id == ^client_id)
    |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_property!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_property(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Property{account_id: account_id}
    |> Property.changeset(attrs)
    |> validate_client_ownership(scope)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a property. When entry method, lockbox code, or alarm code
  change, records an audit entry naming the changed fields (never the
  code values themselves).
  """
  def update_property(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        %Property{} = property,
        attrs
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset =
      property
      |> Property.changeset(attrs)
      |> validate_client_ownership(scope)

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, updated.id)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def change_property(%Scope{}, %Property{} = property, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Property.changeset(property, attrs)
  end

  defp validate_client_ownership(changeset, %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) do
    case Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, :client_id) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      client_id ->
        query = where(Client, [c], c.id == ^client_id and c.account_id == ^account_id)

        if Repo.exists?(query) do
          changeset
        else
          Ecto.Changeset.add_error(changeset, :client_id, "is invalid")
        end
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists audit entries recorded against a property, most recent first.
  """
  def list_property_audit_entries(%Scope{} = scope, %Property{} = property) do
    Recorder.list_for_subject(scope, "Property", property.id)
  end

  defp record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, property_id) do
    changed_fields =
      Property.access_code_fields()
      |> Enum.filter(&Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, &1))
      |> Enum.map(&to_string/1)

    case changed_fields do
      [] ->
        :ok

      fields ->
        Recorder.record(scope, "access_details_updated", "Property", property_id, %{}, %{
          "changed_fields" => fields
        })
    end
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
4	  conflict-aware assignment.
5	
6	  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
7	  """
8	
9	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
10	
11	  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
12	  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
13	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
14	
15	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
16	    AvailabilityBlock,
17	    ConflictDetector,
18	    Job,
19	    Recurrence,
20	    RecurringPlan
21	  }
22	
23	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
24	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User
25	
26	  ## Jobs
27	
28	  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
29	    Job
30	    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
31	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
32	    |> Repo.get!(id)
33	  end
34	
35	  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
36	    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
37	  end
38	
39	  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
40	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
41	    with {:ok, job} <-
42	           %Job{account_id: account_id}
43	           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
44	           |> Repo.insert() do
45	      Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, %{
46	        "scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date),
47	        "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id
48	      })
49	
50	      {:ok, job}
51	    end
52	  end
53	
54	  @doc """
55	  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
56	  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
57	  """
58	  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
59	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
60	    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)
61	
62	    Job
63	    |> where(
64	      [j],
65	      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
66	        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
67	    )
68	    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
69	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
70	    |> Repo.all()
71	  end
72	
73	  @doc """
74	  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
75	  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
76	  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
77	  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
78	  """
79	  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
80	    Job
81	    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
82	    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
83	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
84	    |> Repo.all()
85	  end
86	
87	  @doc """
88	  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
89	  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
90	  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
91	  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
92	  """
93	  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
94	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
95	    with :ok <-
96	           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
97	             scope,
98	             cleaner_id,
99	             job.scheduled_date,
100	             job.start_time,
101	             job.end_time,
102	             exclude_job_id: job.id
103	           ),
104	         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
105	      Recorder.record(
106	        scope,
107	        "job_reassigned",
108	        "Job",
109	        updated.id,
110	        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
111	        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
112	      )
113	
114	      {:ok, updated}
115	    end
116	  end
117	
118	  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
119	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
120	    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
121	      Recorder.record(
122	        scope,
123	        "job_cancelled",
124	        "Job",
125	        updated.id,
126	        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
127	        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
128	      )
129	
130	      {:ok, updated}
131	    end
132	  end
133	
134	  ## Recurring plans
135	
136	  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
137	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
138	    RecurringPlan
139	    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
140	    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
141	    |> Repo.get!(id)
142	  end
143	
144	  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
145	    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
146	  end
147	
148	  @doc """
149	  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
150	  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
151	  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
152	  """
153	  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
154	    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
155	  end
156	
157	  @doc """
158	  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
159	  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
160	  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
161	  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
162	  """
163	  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
164	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
165	    Repo.transact(fn ->
166	      with {:ok, plan} <-
167	             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
168	             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
169	             |> Repo.insert() do
170	        jobs =
171	          plan
172	          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
173	          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
174	            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs)
175	            job
176	          end)
177	
178	        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
179	      end
180	    end)
181	  end
182	
183	  ## Availability blocks
184	
185	  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
186	    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
187	  end
188	
189	  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
190	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
191	    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
192	    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
193	    |> Repo.insert()
194	  end
195	
196	  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)
197	
198	  @doc """
199	  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
200	  assignment pickers.
201	  """
202	  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
203	    scope
204	    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
205	    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
206	  end
207	
208	  @doc """
209	  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
210	  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
211	  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
212	  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
213	  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
214	  through.
215	  """
216	  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
217	      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
218	    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
219	         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
220	      {:ok, user}
221	    end
222	  end
223	
224	  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
225	    %User{}
226	    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
227	    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
228	    |> Repo.insert()
229	  end
230	
231	  defp placeholder_email(name) do
232	    slug =
233	      name
234	      |> String.downcase()
235	      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
236	      |> String.trim(".")
237	
238	    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
239	  end
240	end
241

  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, %{
        "scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date),
        "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id
      })

      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while every other caller (fixtures, other
  # contexts) uses the schema's real field name directly.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

---adr-sms---
# SMS Delivery — Twilio via Req behind a Delivery behaviour

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Stories 837 (client reminders with confirm/reschedule) and 843 (cleaner schedule-change alerts) need reliable SMS. Research flags fragile reminder delivery (blocked numbers, silent failures) as an unresolved incumbent complaint, so delivery status must be tracked per message.

## Options Considered

- **Twilio REST API via Req** — no heavy SDK needed; Req is already a dependency; full delivery-status callbacks.
- **ex_twilio** — wraps the same API but adds a dependency with sporadic maintenance.
- **Telnyx/Plivo** — cheaper per message but smaller ecosystems.

## Decision

Call the Twilio Messages API directly with Req, wrapped in a `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery` behaviour with `Twilio` and `Test` adapters. Persist provider message SIDs and consume Twilio status callbacks to mark delivered/failed on `Notification` records; failures surface in the office delivery log (story 837) and trigger the unacknowledged-alert escalation path (story 843).

## Consequences

- A2P 10DLC registration is required for US SMS; must be documented in deployment runbook.
- Email channel continues through Resend (pre-made ADR); the Delivery behaviour routes per channel.
- Delivery-status webhooks add a public controller endpoint that must verify Twilio signatures.
---adr-oban---
# Background Jobs — Oban

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Several stories need reliable scheduled/asynchronous work: reminder sends ahead of visits (837), recurring-plan job materialization (833), notification delivery with retries (843), invoice generation on completion (836), and payroll export generation (838). Losing a reminder or a materialization run damages exactly the trust this product sells.

## Options Considered

- **Oban** — Postgres-backed, persistent, unique jobs, cron plugin, the community standard.
- **Quantum** — cron scheduling only, no persistence or retries.
- **GenServer + Process.send_after** — no durability across restarts.

## Decision

Use Oban (standard OSS tier) with Postgres. Queues: `notifications`, `scheduling`, `billing`, `exports`. The cron plugin drives daily recurring-plan materialization and reminder scanning; unique-job constraints prevent duplicate reminders per (job, kind).

## Consequences

- Adds `oban` dependency and an Oban migration.
- Workers live inside their owning contexts (e.g. `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler` schedules; a worker performs), keeping Boundary edges clean.
- Test env runs Oban in `:inline`/manual mode for deterministic specs.

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t(),
          slug: String.t() | nil,
          members: [CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          users: [CleanerCrm.Users.User.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @reserved_slugs ~w(admin api www help support docs blog)

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "accounts" do
    field :name, :string
    field :slug, :string

    has_many :members, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member, on_delete: :delete_all
    has_many :users, through: [:members, :user]

    timestamps()
  end

  def changeset(account, attrs) do
    account
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :slug])
    |> validate_required([:name])
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 100)
    |> validate_slug()
    |> unique_constraint(:slug)
  end

  def create_changeset(attrs) do
    %__MODULE__{}
    |> changeset(attrs)
    |> maybe_generate_slug()
  end

  defp validate_slug(changeset) do
    changeset
    |> validate_format(:slug, ~r/^[a-z0-9-]+$/,
      message: "must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens"
    )
    |> validate_length(:slug, min: 3, max: 50)
    |> validate_exclusion(:slug, @reserved_slugs, message: "is reserved and cannot be used")
    |> validate_format(:slug, ~r/^[a-z]/, message: "must start with a letter")
  end

  defp maybe_generate_slug(changeset) do
    case get_field(changeset, :slug) do
      nil ->
        name = get_field(changeset, :name)
        if name, do: put_change(changeset, :slug, generate_slug(name)), else: changeset

      _ ->
        changeset
    end
  end

  defp generate_slug(name) do
    name
    |> String.downcase()
    |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]/, "-")
    |> String.replace(~r/-+/, "-")
    |> String.trim("-")
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts do
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, AccountsRepository, MembersRepository}
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{InvitationRepository, InvitationNotifier}
  alias CleanerCrm.Authorization
  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def subscribe_account(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account")
  end

  def subscribe_member(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member")
  end

  defp broadcast_account(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account", message)
  end

  defp broadcast_member(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member", message)
  end

  def list_accounts(%Scope{} = scope) do
    MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(scope.user.id)
  end

  def get_account(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    case AccountsRepository.get_account(id) do
      nil ->
        nil

      account ->
        case Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account.id) do
          false -> nil
          true -> account
        end
    end
  end

  def get_account!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    account = AccountsRepository.get_account!(id)
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account.id)
    account
  end

  def create_account(%Scope{} = scope, attrs) do
    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.create_account_with_owner(attrs, scope.user.id) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:created, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def update_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.update_account(account, attrs) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:updated, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def delete_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.delete_account(account) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:deleted, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def change_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)
    Account.changeset(account, attrs)
  end

  def list_account_members(%Scope{} = scope, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account_id)
    MembersRepository.list_account_members(account_id)
  end

  def add_user_to_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id, role \\ :member) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.add_user_to_account(user_id, account_id, role) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:created, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def remove_user_from_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_members, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.remove_user_from_account(user_id, account_id) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:deleted, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def update_user_role(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id, role) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_members, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.update_user_role(user_id, account_id, role) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:updated, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def get_user_role(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account_id)
    MembersRepository.get_user_role(user_id, account_id)
  end

  def user_has_account_access?(%Scope{} = scope, account_id) do
    MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(scope.user.id, account_id)
  end

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Invitations
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  def subscribe_invitations(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:invitations")
  end

  defp broadcast_invitation(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:invitations", message)
  end

  def invite_user(scope, account_id, email, role)
      when is_binary(email) and role in [:owner, :admin, :member] and not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id),
         :ok <- validate_user_not_already_member(email, account_id),
         {:ok, invitation} <- create_invitation(scope, account_id, email, role),
         :ok <- send_invitation_email(invitation) do
      broadcast_invitation(scope, {:created, invitation})
      {:ok, invitation}
    end
  end

  def accept_invitation(token, user_attrs) when is_binary(token) and is_map(user_attrs) do
    with {:ok, invitation} <- get_valid_invitation(token),
         {:ok, user} <- resolve_or_create_user(invitation, user_attrs),
         {:ok, member} <- accept_user_to_account(user, invitation),
         {:ok, _updated} <- InvitationRepository.accept(%Scope{}, invitation) do
      {:ok, {user, member}}
    end
  end

  def list_pending_invitations(scope, account_id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    if Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account_id) do
      InvitationRepository.list_pending_invitations(scope, account_id)
    else
      []
    end
  end

  def list_pending_invitations(_scope, nil), do: []

  def get_invitation_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    InvitationRepository.get_by_token_hash(token)
  end

  def cancel_invitation(scope, account_id, invitation_id)
      when is_integer(invitation_id) and not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id),
         invitation when not is_nil(invitation) <-
           InvitationRepository.get_invitation(scope, invitation_id),
         {:ok, cancelled} <- InvitationRepository.cancel(scope, invitation) do
      broadcast_invitation(scope, {:updated, cancelled})
      {:ok, cancelled}
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      error -> error
    end
  end

  def cleanup_expired_invitations do
    InvitationRepository.cleanup_expired_invitations(30)
    :ok
  end

  defp validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id) do
    if Authorization.authorize(:manage_members, scope, account_id),
      do: :ok,
      else: {:error, :not_authorized}
  end

  defp validate_user_not_already_member(email, account_id) do
    case Users.get_user_by_email(email) do
      nil ->
        :ok

      user ->
        if MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(user.id, account_id),
          do: {:error, :user_already_member},
          else: :ok
    end
  end

  defp create_invitation(scope, account_id, email, role) do
    attrs = %{
      email: email,
      role: role,
      account_id: account_id,
      invited_by_user_id: scope.user.id
    }

    InvitationRepository.create_invitation(scope, attrs)
  end

  defp send_invitation_email(invitation) do
    url = CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> "/invitations/accept/#{invitation.token}"

    case InvitationNotifier.deliver_invitation_email(invitation, url) do
      {:ok, _} -> :ok
      {:error, _} -> {:error, :email_delivery_failed}
    end
  end

  defp get_valid_invitation(token) do
    case InvitationRepository.get_by_token_hash(token) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :invalid_token}

      invitation ->
        cond do
          invitation.status != :pending ->
            {:error, :invalid_token}

          DateTime.compare(DateTime.utc_now(), invitation.expires_at) != :lt ->
            {:error, :expired_token}

          true ->
            {:ok, invitation}
        end
    end
  end

  defp resolve_or_create_user(invitation, %{email: provided_email} = user_attrs) do
    if provided_email == invitation.email do
      case Users.get_user_by_email(invitation.email) do
        nil -> Users.register_user(user_attrs)
        existing_user -> {:ok, existing_user}
      end
    else
      {:error, :email_mismatch}
    end
  end

  defp resolve_or_create_user(invitation, user_attrs) do
    user_attrs_with_email = Map.put(user_attrs, :email, invitation.email)

    case Users.get_user_by_email(invitation.email) do
      nil -> Users.register_user(user_attrs_with_email)
      existing_user -> {:ok, existing_user}
    end
  end

  defp accept_user_to_account(user, invitation) do
    inviter = Users.get_user!(invitation.invited_by_user_id)
    inviter_scope = %Scope{user: inviter, active_account_id: invitation.account_id}
    add_user_to_account(inviter_scope, user.id, invitation.account_id, invitation.role)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.UserNotifier do
  import Swoosh.Email

  alias CleanerCrm.Mailer
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  # Delivers the email using the application mailer.
  defp deliver(recipient, subject, body) do
    email =
      new()
      |> to(recipient)
      |> from({"CleanerCrm", "contact@example.com"})
      |> subject(subject)
      |> text_body(body)

    with {:ok, _metadata} <- Mailer.deliver(email) do
      {:ok, email}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Deliver instructions to update a user email.
  """
  def deliver_update_email_instructions(user, url) do
    deliver(user.email, "Update email instructions", """

    ==============================

    Hi #{user.email},

    You can change your email by visiting the URL below:

    #{url}

    If you didn't request this change, please ignore this.

    ==============================
    """)
  end

  @doc """
  Deliver instructions to log in with a magic link.
  """
  def deliver_login_instructions(user, url) do
    case user do
      %User{confirmed_at: nil} -> deliver_confirmation_instructions(user, url)
      _ -> deliver_magic_link_instructions(user, url)
    end
  end

  defp deliver_magic_link_instructions(user, url) do
    deliver(user.email, "Log in instructions", """

    ==============================

    Hi #{user.email},

    You can log into your account by visiting the URL below:

    #{url}

    If you didn't request this email, please ignore this.

    ==============================
    """)
  end

  defp deliver_confirmation_instructions(user, url) do
    deliver(user.email, "Confirmation instructions", """

    ==============================

    Hi #{user.email},

    You can confirm your account by visiting the URL below:

    #{url}

    If you didn't create an account with us, please ignore this.

    ==============================
    """)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb do
  @moduledoc """
  The entrypoint for defining your web interface, such
  as controllers, components, channels, and so on.

  This can be used in your application as:

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller
      use CleanerCrmWeb, :html

  The definitions below will be executed for every controller,
  component, etc, so keep them short and clean, focused
  on imports, uses and aliases.

  Do NOT define functions inside the quoted expressions
  below. Instead, define additional modules and import
  those modules here.
  """

  use Boundary, deps: [CleanerCrm], exports: :all

  def static_paths, do: ~w(assets fonts images favicon.ico robots.txt)

  def router do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Router, helpers: false

      # Import common connection and controller functions to use in pipelines
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.Controller
      import Phoenix.LiveView.Router
    end
  end

  def channel do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Channel
    end
  end

  def controller do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Controller, formats: [:html, :json]

      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      import Plug.Conn

      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def live_view do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveView

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def live_component do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveComponent

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def html do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Component

      # Import convenience functions from controllers
      import Phoenix.Controller,
        only: [get_csrf_token: 0, view_module: 1, view_template: 1]

      # Include general helpers for rendering HTML
      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  defp html_helpers do
    quote do
      # Translation
      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      # HTML escaping functionality
      import Phoenix.HTML
      # Core UI components
      import CleanerCrmWeb.CoreComponents

      # Common modules used in templates
      alias Phoenix.LiveView.JS
      alias CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts

      # Routes generation with the ~p sigil
      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def verified_routes do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.VerifiedRoutes,
        endpoint: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
        router: CleanerCrmWeb.Router,
        statics: CleanerCrmWeb.static_paths()
    end
  end

  @doc """
  When used, dispatch to the appropriate controller/live_view/etc.
  """
  defmacro __using__(which) when is_atom(which) do
    apply(__MODULE__, which, [])
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.Scope do
  @moduledoc """
  Defines the scope of the caller to be used throughout the app.

  The `CleanerCrm.Users.Scope` allows public interfaces to receive
  information about the caller, such as if the call is initiated from an
  end-user, and if so, which user. Additionally, such a scope can carry fields
  such as "super user" or other privileges for use in authorization checks,
  or to ensure specific code paths can only be accessed for a given scope.

  It is useful for logging as well as for scoping pubsub subscriptions and
  broadcasts when a caller subscribes to an interface or performs a particular
  action.

  Feel free to extend the fields on this struct to fit the needs of
  growing application requirements.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  defstruct user: nil,
            active_account: nil,
            active_account_id: nil

  @doc """
  Creates a scope for the given user.

  Returns nil if no user is given.
  """
  def for_user(%User{} = user) do
    %__MODULE__{user: user}
  end

  def for_user(nil), do: nil
end

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines the test case to be used by
  tests that require setting up a connection.

  Such tests rely on `Phoenix.ConnTest` and also
  import other functionality to make it easier
  to build common data structures and query the data layer.

  Finally, if the test case interacts with the database,
  we enable the SQL sandbox, so changes done to the database
  are reverted at the end of every test. If you are using
  PostgreSQL, you can even run database tests asynchronously
  by setting `use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true`, although
  this option is not recommended for other databases.
  """

  use ExUnit.CaseTemplate

  using do
    quote do
      # The default endpoint for testing
      @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

      # Import conveniences for testing with connections
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.ConnTest
      import CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase
    end
  end

  setup tags do
    CleanerCrmTest.DataCase.setup_sandbox(tags)
    {:ok, conn: Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()}
  end

  @doc """
  Setup helper that registers and logs in users.

      setup :register_and_log_in_user

  It stores an updated connection and a registered user in the
  test context.
  """
  def register_and_log_in_user(%{conn: conn} = context) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = CleanerCrm.Users.Scope.for_user(user)

    opts =
      context
      |> Map.take([:token_authenticated_at])
      |> Enum.into([])

    %{conn: log_in_user(conn, user, opts), user: user, scope: scope}
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the given `user` into the `conn`.

  It returns an updated `conn`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, opts \\ []) do
    token = CleanerCrm.Users.generate_user_session_token(user)

    maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, opts[:token_authenticated_at])

    conn
    |> Phoenix.ConnTest.init_test_session(%{})
    |> Plug.Conn.put_session(:user_token, token)
  end

  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(_token, nil), do: nil

  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) do
    CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines test helpers for creating
  entities via the `CleanerCrm.Users` context.
  """

  import Ecto.Query

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def unique_user_email, do: "user#{System.unique_integer()}@example.com"
  def valid_user_password, do: "hello world!"

  def valid_user_attributes(attrs \\ %{}) do
    Enum.into(attrs, %{
      email: unique_user_email()
    })
  end

  def unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, user} =
      attrs
      |> valid_user_attributes()
      |> Users.register_user()

    user
  end

  def user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs)

    token =
      extract_user_token(fn url ->
        Users.deliver_login_instructions(user, url)
      end)

    {:ok, {user, _expired_tokens}} =
      Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)

    user
  end

  def user_scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    user_scope_fixture(user)
  end

  def user_scope_fixture(user) do
    Scope.for_user(user)
  end

  def set_password(user) do
    {:ok, {user, _expired_tokens}} =
      Users.update_user_password(user, %{password: valid_user_password()})

    user
  end

  def extract_user_token(fun) do
    {:ok, captured_email} = fun.(&"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")
    [_, token | _] = String.split(captured_email.text_body, "[TOKEN]")
    token
  end

  def override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) when is_binary(token) do
    CleanerCrm.Repo.update_all(
      from(t in Users.UserToken,
        where: t.token == ^token
      ),
      set: [authenticated_at: authenticated_at]
    )
  end

  def generate_user_magic_link_token(user) do
    {encoded_token, user_token} = Users.UserToken.build_email_token(user, "login")
    CleanerCrm.Repo.insert!(user_token)
    {encoded_token, user_token.token}
  end

  def offset_user_token(token, amount_to_add, unit) do
    dt = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(:second), amount_to_add, unit)

    CleanerCrm.Repo.update_all(
      from(ut in Users.UserToken, where: ut.token == ^token),
      set: [inserted_at: dt, authenticated_at: dt]
    )
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens do
  @moduledoc """
  Shared givens for Cleaner CRM BDD specs.

  Consumer spex modules pull these in with a plain Elixir `import`:

      import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

      scenario "..." do
        given_ :logged_in_owner_with_account
      end

  | Name | Produces | Requires |
  |---|---|---|
  | `:logged_in_owner_with_account` | `context.conn` (authenticated), `context.user`, `context.scope`, `context.account` | `context.conn` |
  """

  use SexySpex.Givens

  import Phoenix.ConnTest
  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint

  register_given :logged_in_owner_with_account, context do
    user = Fixtures.user_fixture() |> Fixtures.set_password()
    scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
    account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

    {:ok, login_live, _html} = live(context.conn, "/users/log-in")

    form =
      form(login_live, "#login_form_password",
        user: %{
          email: user.email,
          password: Fixtures.valid_user_password(),
          remember_me: true
        }
      )

    conn = submit_form(form, context.conn)

    {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story832.Criterion7107Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 832 — Manage clients and properties with access details
  Criterion 7107 — Adding a property under an existing client saves it
  and lists it under that client as its only owning client.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "owner adds a property to an existing client" do
    scenario "the property is saved and listed under its client" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client \"Sarah Kim\" exists", context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Sarah Kim")
        {:ok, Map.put(context, :client_path, client_path)}
      end

      when_ "the owner adds a property \"123 Oak St\" and assigns it to Sarah Kim", context do
        property_path =
          create_property(context.conn, context.client_path, %{service_address: "123 Oak St"})

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :property_path, property_path)}
      end

      then_ "the property is saved and listed under Sarah Kim", context do
        {:ok, _client_live, html} = live(context.conn, context.client_path)
        assert html =~ "123 Oak St"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the property shows Sarah Kim as its only owning client", context do
        {:ok, property_live, html} = live(context.conn, context.property_path)

        assert has_element?(property_live, "[data-test='property-client']", "Sarah Kim")
        assert length(Regex.scan(~r/data-test="property-client"/, html)) == 1

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp create_client(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='client-form']", client: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_property(conn, client_path, attrs) do
    "/clients/" <> client_id = client_path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story836.Criterion7153Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 836 — Invoice completed jobs and collect payment
  Criterion 7153 — Completing a job generates its invoice
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "marking a job complete generates its invoice" do
    scenario "completing a job generates its invoice" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a scheduled job has an agreed price of $150", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
            status: :scheduled
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the cleaner marks the job complete", context do
        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        job_live
        |> element("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")
        |> render_click()

input.message:
Heads up before I dig in further: confirmed (by running test/spex/836's own criterion_7153 spex) that the standard given_ block used by stories 836, 837, and ~28 other call sites across untouched stories has a bug — `scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user); account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)` never refreshes `scope.active_account_id`, so any later `Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, ...)` / `job_fixture(context.scope, ...)` crashes with FunctionClauseError in Clients/Scheduling (both require non-nil active_account_id). Story 834's spex files already work around this correctly with `scope = %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}` — 836/837/838/839 etc. don't.

I can't fix this in CleanerCrm.Scheduling (forbidden to me) and won't touch the sealed spex files. My plan: add a small `ensure_active_account/1` fallback helper inside test/support/fixtures/cleaner_crm_spex_fixtures.ex (looks up the user's account via CleanerCrm.Accounts.list_accounts when active_account_id is nil) and call it at the top of client_fixture/job_fixture/notification_fixture/etc. This only activates on the nil-fallback path, so it's a no-op wherever scope is already refreshed — safe for other stories, and unblocks 837 without touching Scheduling/Clients/Audit. Flagging since whoever owns Billing/TimeTracking/Quality (836/838/839) will hit the identical crash. Proceeding with implementation now.
