defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Application do
  # See https://elixir.hexdocs.pm/Application.html
  # for more information on OTP Applications
  @moduledoc false

  use Application

  @impl true
  def start(_type, _args) do
    children = [
      CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry,
      CleanerCrm.Repo,
      {DNSCluster, query: Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, :dns_cluster_query) || :ignore},
      {Phoenix.PubSub, name: CleanerCrm.PubSub},
      CleanerCrm.Vault,
      CleanerCrm.Integrations.OAuthStateStore,
      # Start a worker by calling: CleanerCrm.Worker.start_link(arg)
      # {CleanerCrm.Worker, arg},
      # Start to serve requests, typically the last entry
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint
    ]

    # See https://elixir.hexdocs.pm/Supervisor.html
    # for other strategies and supported options
    opts = [strategy: :one_for_one, name: CleanerCrm.Supervisor]
    Supervisor.start_link(children, opts)
  end

  # Tell Phoenix to update the endpoint configuration
  # whenever the application is updated.
  @impl true
  def config_change(changed, _new, removed) do
    CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.config_change(changed, removed)
    :ok
  end
end

import Config

# config/runtime.exs is executed for all environments, including
# during releases. It is executed after compilation and before the
# system starts, so it is typically used to load production configuration
# and secrets from environment variables or elsewhere. Do not define
# any compile-time configuration in here, as it won't be applied.
# The block below contains prod specific runtime configuration.

# ## Using releases
#
# If you use `mix release`, you need to explicitly enable the server
# by passing the PHX_SERVER=true when you start it:
#
#     PHX_SERVER=true bin/cleaner_crm start
#
# Alternatively, you can use `mix phx.gen.release` to generate a `bin/server`
# script that automatically sets the env var above.
if System.get_env("PHX_SERVER") do
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint, server: true
end

config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  http: [port: String.to_integer(System.get_env("PORT", "4100"))]

# CodeMySpec feedback widget / OAuth provider credentials.
# Generate the client ID/secret on the CodeMySpec project page and set them
# as env vars before deploying.
config :cleaner_crm,
  codemyspec_url: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_URL") || "https://codemyspec.com",
  codemyspec_client_id: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_CLIENT_ID"),
  codemyspec_client_secret: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_CLIENT_SECRET")

if config_env() == :prod do
  # Encrypted-token vault key — required in production.
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Vault,
    ciphers: [
      default:
        {Cloak.Ciphers.AES.GCM,
         tag: "AES.GCM.V1",
         key:
           Base.decode64!(
             System.get_env("CLOAK_KEY") ||
               raise("environment variable CLOAK_KEY is missing (base64 32-byte key)")
           )}
    ]
end

if config_env() == :prod do
  database_url =
    System.get_env("DATABASE_URL") ||
      raise """
      environment variable DATABASE_URL is missing.
      For example: ecto://USER:PASS@HOST/DATABASE
      """

  maybe_ipv6 = if System.get_env("ECTO_IPV6") in ~w(true 1), do: [:inet6], else: []

  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Repo,
    # ssl: true,
    url: database_url,
    pool_size: String.to_integer(System.get_env("POOL_SIZE") || "10"),
    # For machines with several cores, consider starting multiple pools of `pool_size`
    # pool_count: 4,
    socket_options: maybe_ipv6

  # The secret key base is used to sign/encrypt cookies and other secrets.
  # A default value is used in config/dev.exs and config/test.exs but you
  # want to use a different value for prod and you most likely don't want
  # to check this value into version control, so we use an environment
  # variable instead.
  secret_key_base =
    System.get_env("SECRET_KEY_BASE") ||
      raise """
      environment variable SECRET_KEY_BASE is missing.
      You can generate one by calling: mix phx.gen.secret
      """

  host = System.get_env("PHX_HOST") || "example.com"

  config :cleaner_crm, :dns_cluster_query, System.get_env("DNS_CLUSTER_QUERY")

  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
    url: [host: host, port: 443, scheme: "https"],
    http: [
      # Enable IPv6 and bind on all interfaces.
      # Set it to  {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1} for local network only access.
      # See the documentation on https://bandit.hexdocs.pm/Bandit.html#t:options/0
      # for details about using IPv6 vs IPv4 and loopback vs public addresses.
      ip: {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
    ],
    secret_key_base: secret_key_base

  # ## SSL Support
  #
  # To get SSL working, you will need to add the `https` key
  # to your endpoint configuration:
  #
  #     config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  #       https: [
  #         ...,
  #         port: 443,
  #         cipher_suite: :strong,
  #         keyfile: System.get_env("SOME_APP_SSL_KEY_PATH"),
  #         certfile: System.get_env("SOME_APP_SSL_CERT_PATH")
  #       ]
  #
  # The `cipher_suite` is set to `:strong` to support only the
  # latest and more secure SSL ciphers. This means old browsers
  # and clients may not be supported. You can set it to
  # `:compatible` for wider support.
  #
  # `:keyfile` and `:certfile` expect an absolute path to the key
  # and cert in disk or a relative path inside priv, for example
  # "priv/ssl/server.key". For all supported SSL configuration
  # options, see https://plug.hexdocs.pm/Plug.SSL.html#configure/1
  #
  # We also recommend setting `force_ssl` in your config/prod.exs,
  # ensuring no data is ever sent via http, always redirecting to https:
  #
  #     config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  #       force_ssl: [hsts: true]
  #
  # Check `Plug.SSL` for all available options in `force_ssl`.

  # ## Configuring the mailer
  #
  # In production you need to configure the mailer to use a different adapter.
  # Here is an example configuration for Mailgun:
  #
  #     config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Mailer,
  #       adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Mailgun,
  #       api_key: System.get_env("MAILGUN_API_KEY"),
  #       domain: System.get_env("MAILGUN_DOMAIN")
  #
  # Most non-SMTP adapters require an API client. Swoosh supports Req, Hackney,
  # and Finch out-of-the-box. This configuration is typically done at
  # compile-time in your config/prod.exs:
  #
  #     config :swoosh, :api_client, Swoosh.ApiClient.Req
  #
  # See https://swoosh.hexdocs.pm/Swoosh.html#module-installation for details.
end

# Recurrence Engine & Timezones — project-local recurrence with materialized jobs, tzdata

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Story 833 is the product's differentiator: recurring plans with conflict detection across the entire series, not just the first visit (the named ZenMaid gap). Story 846 layers preferred-cleaner defaults onto generated visits. Cleaning cadences are simple (weekly/biweekly/every-4-weeks, fixed weekday/time), not arbitrary RFC 5545 RRULEs.

## Options Considered

- **Project-local recurrence module + materialized Job rows** — generate concrete jobs N weeks ahead (Oban cron); conflict detection becomes plain SQL over real rows.
- **RRULE library (e.g. `cocktail`)** — full RFC 5545 power we don't need; conflict detection against virtual occurrences is much harder than against rows.
- **Virtual occurrences computed on read** — no rows to detect conflicts against; breaks the core story.

## Decision

Write `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence` as project-local code generating a 12-week rolling horizon of `Job` rows from each `RecurringPlan` (extended by a daily Oban job). `ConflictDetector` runs SQL overlap queries across the whole materialized series against jobs and availability blocks. Times are stored UTC; each Company has an IANA timezone (via `tzdata` + `DateTime.shift_zone/2`) used for materialization and display, keeping visits pinned to local wall-clock across DST.

## Consequences

- Adds `tzdata` dependency and a `timezone` field on Company.
- Plan edits must reconcile already-materialized future jobs (regenerate unstarted ones, flag manually-modified ones) — this logic lives in `Scheduling` and needs careful spec coverage.
- 12-week horizon bounds conflict detection; conflicts beyond the horizon surface as the horizon rolls forward.

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients.Client do
  @moduledoc """
  A paying customer with contact info and preferences.

  Scoped to an account: every client belongs to exactly one account and
  is only ever visible within that account.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t() | nil,
          active: boolean(),
          card_on_file: boolean(),
          properties: [CleanerCrm.Clients.Property.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "clients" do
    field :name, :string
    field :active, :boolean, default: true
    field :card_on_file, :boolean, default: false

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    has_many :properties, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(client, attrs) do
    client
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :active, :card_on_file])
    |> validate_required([:name], message: "is required")
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 200)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Curated bridge from BDD specs into in-app state.

  The only module that may dep on `CleanerCrm` from inside the spex test
  tree. Declared as its own top-level Boundary so the spec boundary
  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.

  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
  """

  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]

  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
            [
              CleanerCrm.Clients,
              CleanerCrm.Scheduling,
              CleanerCrm.Billing,
              CleanerCrm.Notifications
            ]}

  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
    user
  end

  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
  #
  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false
        })
      )

    client
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled,
          scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
          start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
          end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
        })
      )

    job
  end

  # `given_` blocks bind `scope` from `user_scope_fixture/1` *before*
  # `account_fixture/2` creates the account, so it never carries an
  # `active_account_id` — every fixture below that scopes a context
  # call by account needs to resolve it from the user's membership at
  # call time instead of trusting the scope it was handed.
  defp scoped_to_account(%CleanerCrm.Users.Scope{active_account_id: nil, user: user} = scope) do
    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(user.id) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  defp scoped_to_account(scope), do: scope

  def job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)
    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })
      )

    invoice
  end

  # Time tracking (story 838) — a resolved clock-in/out record for a
  # job.
  #
  # Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  # 838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job). Scenarios whose subject is a downstream pay
  # calculation (hourly vs. piece-rate, running pay-period totals,
  # payroll CSV export) seed the resolved time entry directly here
  # instead of re-driving the clock-in/out flow every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, time_entry} =
      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })
      )

    time_entry
  end

  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder
  # with its confirm/reschedule token.
  #
  # The automatic "reminder sent at the configured lead time" trigger
  # is covered end-to-end by story 837's own "reminder fires at the
  # configured lead time" spec. Scenarios whose subject is a
  # downstream decision on an existing reminder (confirm, reschedule,
  # delivery-status fallback) seed the already-sent notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the scheduler trigger every
  # time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def notification_fixture(scope, client, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :reminder,
          channel: :email,
          status: :sent,
          token: "reminder_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change
  # notification already pushed to a cleaner.
  #
  # The push itself (a moved or cancelled job creating this
  # notification) is covered end-to-end by story 843's own "moved job
  # notifies the cleaner" / "cancelled job notifies the cleaner"
  # specs, which drive the real trigger via `ScheduleLive.Board`.
  # Scenarios whose subject is a downstream decision on an existing
  # pending change (acknowledging, re-prompting, office visibility,
  # escalation, channel fallback) seed the already-pushed notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the board move every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md. Never pass
  # `status: :acknowledged` here — the acknowledgment round-trip
  # through `FieldLive.Today` is the whole point of story 843.
  def schedule_change_notification_fixture(scope, cleaner, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :schedule_change,
          channel: :push,
          status: :pending,
          change_summary: "Job schedule changed",
          pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          token: "schedule_change_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Quality (story 839) — a job carrying an unfinished, per-job
  # checklist of required and optional tasks.
  #
  # Checking items off and completing the job through the checklist UI
  # is the subject under test in `FieldLive.Job`, so this fixture stops
  # short of that — it only seeds the checklist itself. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md: `ChecklistTemplate` assignment
  # (story 842) has its own creation flow this fixture skips.
  def job_with_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)

    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
        %{task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true},
        %{task: "Fridge interior wiped down", required: false}
      ])

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Quality (story 842) — a job carrying an unfinished, room-grouped

  def job_with_room_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, items, attrs \\ %{}) do

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications.Notification do
  @moduledoc """
  An outbound message — a client appointment reminder or a cleaner
  schedule-change alert — with delivery status and acknowledgment
  tracking.

  `kind: :reminder` notifications carry a `client_id` and move through
  `:sent -> :delivered | :undelivered -> :confirmed | :reschedule_requested`.
  `kind: :schedule_change` notifications carry a `cleaner_id` instead
  and move through `:pending -> :acknowledged` (or `:escalated` when
  never acknowledged in time).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @kinds [:reminder, :schedule_change]
  @channels [:email, :sms, :push]
  @statuses [
    :pending,
    :sent,
    :delivered,
    :undelivered,
    :failed,
    :confirmed,
    :reschedule_requested,
    :acknowledged,
    :escalated
  ]

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          kind: :reminder | :schedule_change,
          channel: :email | :sms | :push,
          status: atom(),
          token: String.t() | nil,
          provider_message_id: String.t() | nil,
          failure_reason: String.t() | nil,
          change_summary: String.t() | nil,
          pushed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          sent_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          delivered_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          confirmed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          acknowledged_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          escalated_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "notifications" do
    field :kind, Ecto.Enum, values: @kinds
    field :channel, Ecto.Enum, values: @channels
    field :status, Ecto.Enum, values: @statuses, default: :pending
    field :token, :string
    field :provider_message_id, :string
    field :failure_reason, :string
    field :change_summary, :string

    field :pushed_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :sent_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :delivered_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :confirmed_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :reschedule_requested_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :acknowledged_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :escalated_at, :utc_datetime_usec

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id cleaner_id job_id kind channel status token provider_message_id
             failure_reason change_summary pushed_at sent_at delivered_at confirmed_at
             reschedule_requested_at acknowledged_at escalated_at)a

  def changeset(notification, attrs) do
    notification
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:job_id, :kind, :channel, :token])
    |> unique_constraint(:token)
    |> foreign_key_constraint(:job_id)
  end

  def kinds, do: @kinds
  def channels, do: @channels
  def statuses, do: @statuses
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Twilio do
  @moduledoc """
  Sends SMS via the Twilio Messages REST API using `Req` directly —
  no `ex_twilio` dependency, per the sms-delivery ADR. Configured via
  `config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery.Twilio,
  account_sid:, auth_token:, from_number:, status_callback_url:`.
  """

  @behaviour CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery

  @impl true
  def send_sms(phone, body) do
    config = Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, __MODULE__, [])
    account_sid = Keyword.fetch!(config, :account_sid)
    auth_token = Keyword.fetch!(config, :auth_token)
    from_number = Keyword.fetch!(config, :from_number)

    form =
      %{"To" => phone, "From" => from_number, "Body" => body}
      |> maybe_put_status_callback(config[:status_callback_url])

    [base_url: "https://api.twilio.com/2010-04-01", auth: {:basic, "#{account_sid}:#{auth_token}"}]
    |> Req.new()
    |> Req.post(url: "/Accounts/#{account_sid}/Messages.json", form: form)
    |> handle_response()
  end

  defp maybe_put_status_callback(form, nil), do: form
  defp maybe_put_status_callback(form, url), do: Map.put(form, "StatusCallback", url)

  defp handle_response({:ok, %Req.Response{status: 201, body: %{"sid" => sid}}}),
    do: {:ok, %{provider_message_id: sid}}

  defp handle_response({:ok, %Req.Response{status: status, body: body}}),
    do: {:error, {status, body}}

  defp handle_response({:error, reason}), do: {:error, reason}
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler do
  @moduledoc """
  Schedules reminder sends ahead of upcoming jobs.

  Driven by Oban's cron plugin in production (see the
  background-jobs-oban ADR): `perform/1` runs on a schedule and calls
  `scan_and_send/1`, the pure entry point, so the same check can also
  be run synchronously — deterministic, no clock-waiting — right after
  a job is created.

  Only accounts that have explicitly saved reminder settings
  (`CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderLive`) are scanned, so this never fires for
  an account that hasn't opted in.
  """

  use Oban.Worker, queue: :notifications

  import Ecto.Query

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{Delivery, Notification, ReminderNotifier, ReminderSettings}

  @impl Oban.Worker
  def perform(%Oban.Job{}) do
    scan_and_send()
    :ok
  end

  @doc "Sends every reminder that's due right now, across every account with reminder settings."
  def scan_and_send(now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    ReminderSettings
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.each(&send_for_account(&1, now))
  end

  defp send_for_account(%ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id, lead_time_hours: lead_time_hours}, now) do
    account_id
    |> due_jobs()
    |> Enum.filter(&due_now?(&1, lead_time_hours, now))
    |> Enum.each(&send_reminder/1)
  end

  defp due_jobs(account_id) do
    already_reminded =
      from n in Notification, where: n.job_id == parent_as(:job).id and n.kind == :reminder

    from(j in Job,
      as: :job,
      where: j.account_id == ^account_id,
      where: j.status == :scheduled,
      where: not is_nil(j.client_id),
      where: not exists(already_reminded),
      preload: [:client]
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp due_now?(%Job{scheduled_date: date, start_time: time}, lead_time_hours, now) do
    with {:ok, start_at} <- DateTime.new(date, time, "Etc/UTC") do
      due_at = DateTime.add(start_at, -lead_time_hours * 3600, :second)
      DateTime.compare(due_at, now) != :gt and DateTime.compare(start_at, now) == :gt
    else
      _ -> false
    end
  end

  defp send_reminder(%Job{client: %Client{preferred_channel: :sms, phone: phone}} = job)
       when is_binary(phone) do
    token = CleanerCrm.Notifications.generate_token()
    body = reminder_sms_body(job, token)

    case Delivery.send_sms(phone, body) do
      {:ok, %{provider_message_id: sid}} ->
        insert_notification!(job, job.client, :sms, token, sid, DateTime.utc_now())

      {:error, _reason} ->
        send_email_reminder(job, job.client)
    end
  end

  defp send_reminder(%Job{client: client} = job), do: send_email_reminder(job, client)

  defp send_email_reminder(job, client) do
    token = CleanerCrm.Notifications.generate_token()
    confirm_url = reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")
    reschedule_url = reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")

    {:ok, _email} = ReminderNotifier.deliver_reminder(client, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url)

    insert_notification!(job, client, :email, token, nil, DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  defp reminder_sms_body(job, token) do
    "Cleaning appointment reminder for #{job.scheduled_date} at #{job.start_time}. " <>
      "Confirm: #{reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")} " <>
      "Reschedule: #{reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")}"
  end

  defp insert_notification!(job, client, channel, token, provider_message_id, sent_at) do
    %Notification{account_id: job.account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(%{
      client_id: client.id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :reminder,
      channel: channel,
      status: :sent,
      token: token,
      provider_message_id: provider_message_id,
      sent_at: sent_at
    })
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp reminder_url(path), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> path
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
  @moduledoc """
  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{Notification, ReminderNotifier, ReminderScheduler, ReminderSettings}

  ## Reminder settings

  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings
    end
  end

  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
  end

  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_reminder_settings()
    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  @doc "Runs the periodic reminder scan now — see `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler`."
  defdelegate send_due_reminders(), to: ReminderScheduler, as: :scan_and_send

  ## Notifications

  def create_notification(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Notification{account_id: account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "The office's delivery log: every notification for the account, most recent first."
  def list_notifications(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> preload([:client, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Public confirm/reschedule — reached by token, no scope available

  def get_notification_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Repo.get_by(Notification, token: token)
  end

  def confirm_reminder(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :confirmed, confirmed_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  def request_reschedule(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :reschedule_requested, reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "True once the client has confirmed the most recent reminder sent for this job."
  def job_confirmed?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :confirmed)
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc "True once the client has asked to reschedule via the most recent reminder for this job."
  def reschedule_requested?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :reschedule_requested)
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  ## Twilio delivery-status webhook

  @doc """
  Applies a Twilio status callback: marks the matching notification
  delivered or undelivered, and — for an undeliverable SMS reminder —
  falls back to emailing the client and flags it for office visibility.
  """

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do

  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings
    end
  end

  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
  end

  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_reminder_settings()
    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  defdelegate send_due_reminders(), to: ReminderScheduler, as: :scan_and_send

  ## Notifications

  def create_notification(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Notification{account_id: account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "The office's delivery log: every notification for the account, most recent first."
  def list_notifications(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id)

  # See https://elixir.hexdocs.pm/Application.html
  # for more information on OTP Applications
  @moduledoc false

  use Application

  @impl true
  def start(_type, _args) do
    children = [
      CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry,
      CleanerCrm.Repo,
      {DNSCluster, query: Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, :dns_cluster_query) || :ignore},
      {Phoenix.PubSub, name: CleanerCrm.PubSub},
      CleanerCrm.Vault,
      CleanerCrm.Integrations.OAuthStateStore,
      # Start a worker by calling: CleanerCrm.Worker.start_link(arg)
      # {CleanerCrm.Worker, arg},
      # Start to serve requests, typically the last entry
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint
    ]

    # See https://elixir.hexdocs.pm/Supervisor.html
    # for other strategies and supported options
    opts = [strategy: :one_for_one, name: CleanerCrm.Supervisor]
    Supervisor.start_link(children, opts)
  end

  # Tell Phoenix to update the endpoint configuration
  # whenever the application is updated.
  @impl true
  def config_change(changed, _new, removed) do
    CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.config_change(changed, removed)
    :ok
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderLive do @moduledoc """ Office configuration of reminder timing and a delivery log showing every send and its status — including failed sends the office needs to follow up on. Route: `/reminders`. """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Notifications @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header> Reminders <:subtitle>Timing and delivery log <.form for={@settings_form} id="reminder-settings-form" data-test="reminder-settings-form" phx-submit="save_settings" > <.input field={@settings_form[:lead_time_hours]} type="number" label="Send reminders this many hours before the appointment" /> <.button type="submit" phx-disable-with="Saving...">Save <.header class="mt-8">Delivery log
{contact(notification)} {channel_label(notification.channel)} {to_string(notification.status)}
""" end @impl true def mount(_params, _session, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope {:ok, socket |> assign(:settings_form, settings_form(scope)) |> assign(:notifications, Notifications.list_notifications(scope))} end @impl true def handle_event("save_settings", %{"settings" => params}, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope case Notifications.update_reminder_settings(scope, params) do {:ok, _settings} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :settings_form, settings_form(scope))} {:error, changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :settings_form, to_form(changeset, as: :settings))} end end defp settings_form(scope) do scope |> Notifications.change_reminder_settings() |> to_form(as: :settings) end defp contact(%{client: %CleanerCrm.Clients.Client{} = client}) do [client.phone, client.email] |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1) |> Enum.join(" / ") end defp contact(_notification), do: "" defp channel_label(:sms), do: "SMS" defp channel_label(:email), do: "Email" defp channel_label(:push), do: "Push" end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderController do
  @moduledoc """
  Public confirm/reschedule endpoints clients reach from reminder
  messages — reached by the opaque token in the link, no
  authentication.
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications

  def confirm(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
    case Notifications.confirm_reminder(token) do
      {:ok, _notification} -> render(conn, :confirm)
      {:error, :not_found} -> conn |> put_status(:not_found) |> render(:not_found)
    end
  end

  def reschedule(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
    case Notifications.request_reschedule(token) do
      {:ok, _notification} -> render(conn, :reschedule)
      {:error, :not_found} -> conn |> put_status(:not_found) |> render(:not_found)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.TwilioWebhookController do
  @moduledoc """
  Twilio's delivery-status callback for outbound SMS reminders and
  cleaner alerts. Always acks 200 so Twilio doesn't retry, regardless
  of whether the message SID matched a notification we sent.
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications

  def status(conn, params) do
    Notifications.handle_delivery_status(params)
    json(conn, %{ok: true})
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — `/pay/:token` is reached by a client
  # with no session and no CSRF token (from a mailed or shared link),
  # and no `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` — there is no logged-in user
  # to scope against on this public page.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PaymentController do
  @moduledoc """
  Public payment-link pages: a client without a card on file reaches
  `/pay/:token` (the link `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show` sends) to
  pay an invoice directly, no login required.

  ## Dependencies

  - `CleanerCrm.Billing`
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing

  def show(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
    case Billing.get_invoice_by_token(token) do
      nil -> render_not_found(conn)
      invoice -> render(conn, :show, invoice: invoice)
    end
  end

  def create(conn, %{"token" => token} = params) do
    case Billing.get_invoice_by_token(token) do
      nil -> render_not_found(conn)
      invoice -> submit_payment(conn, invoice, params)
    end
  end

  defp submit_payment(conn, invoice, params) do
    payment_method = Map.get(params, "payment_method")
    save_card = Map.get(params, "save_card") in ["true", "on"]

    case Billing.pay_via_link(invoice, payment_method) do
      {:ok, updated} -> render(conn, :paid, invoice: updated, save_card: save_card)
      {:error, _reason} -> render(conn, :declined, invoice: invoice)
    end
  end

  defp render_not_found(conn) do
    conn
    |> put_status(:not_found)
    |> render(:not_found)
  end
end

mix spex

Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve
as both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development
workflows.

Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup
blocks:

  * setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
  * setup: State reset between tests
  * Context passing between test steps
  * Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

## Usage

    mix spex                    # Run all spex files
    mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
    mix spex --help             # Show this help

    --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
    --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
    --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
    --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
    --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow

defmodule Mix.Tasks.Spex do
  @shortdoc "Run executable specifications (spex)"
  @moduledoc """
  Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

  SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve as
  both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development workflows.

  Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup blocks:
  - setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
  - setup: State reset between tests
  - Context passing between test steps
  - Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

  ## Usage

      mix spex                    # Run all spex files
      mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
  @moduledoc """
  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{Notification, ReminderNotifier, ReminderScheduler, ReminderSettings}

  ## Reminder settings

  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings
    end
  end

  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
  end

  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_reminder_settings()
    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  @doc "Runs the periodic reminder scan now — see `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler`."
  defdelegate send_due_reminders(), to: ReminderScheduler, as: :scan_and_send

  ## Notifications

  def create_notification(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Notification{account_id: account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "The office's delivery log: every notification for the account, most recent first."
  def list_notifications(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do

  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{Notification, ReminderNotifier, ReminderScheduler, ReminderSettings}

    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings
    end
  end

  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
  end

      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_reminder_settings()
    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  ## Notifications

      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Notification{account_id: account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "The office's delivery log: every notification for the account, most recent first."
  def list_notifications(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> preload([:client, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  reminder for this job, for `ScheduleLive.Index` to render on the
  board — `nil` (no decision yet), `:confirmed`, or
  `:reschedule_requested`.

    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder)
    |> where([n], n.status in [:confirmed, :reschedule_requested])

       when not is_nil(client_id) do

    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, notification.job_id)

    reschedule_url = reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")

    {:ok, _email} = ReminderNotifier.deliver_reminder(client, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url)

    %Notification{account_id: notification.account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(%{

      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :reminder,

      token: token,
      sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()

    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(_notification), do: :ok

  ## Schedule-change alerts (story 843 groundwork)

  def acknowledge(token) when is_binary(token) do

  def list_unacknowledged(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do

content.text:
## Summary

I implemented the Notifications slice for story 837 (plus schema groundwork for 843) in `/Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm`.

**Files created:**
- `lib/cleaner_crm/notifications.ex` — public context API (reminder settings, notification CRUD, confirm/reschedule by token, Twilio webhook handling, schedule-change acknowledgment groundwork)
- `lib/cleaner_crm/notifications/notification.ex`, `reminder_settings.ex` — schemas
- `lib/cleaner_crm/notifications/reminder_scheduler.ex` — Oban worker that scans for due reminders
- `lib/cleaner_crm/notifications/reminder_notifier.ex` — Swoosh email builder
- `lib/cleaner_crm/notifications/delivery.ex` + `delivery/twilio.ex` + `delivery/test.ex` — SMS delivery behaviour and adapters (Req-based, no `ex_twilio`)
- `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/reminder_live.ex`, `controllers/reminder_controller.ex` (+ HTML templates), `controllers/twilio_webhook_controller.ex`
- Migrations for `notifications`, `reminder_settings`, Oban's job table, and `clients.preferred_channel`

**Files modified:** `mix.exs`, `config/{config,test,runtime}.exs`, `lib/cleaner_crm_web/application.ex`, `lib/cleaner_crm.ex` (boundary exports), `router.ex`, `lib/cleaner_crm/clients/client.ex`, and `test/support/fixtures/cleaner_crm_spex_fixtures.ex` (fixed a shared scope bug and a default-`end_time` bug affecting multiple stories' fixtures, not just mine).

**Test results:** Story 837 passes 4 of 6 criteria (7183, 7185, 7186, 7189). The remaining two (7187 confirm, 7188 reschedule) fail only on their second assertion, which checks that `ScheduleLive.Index` — a file I'm explicitly barred from touching — renders "Confirmed"/"Needs reschedule" on the board. I added `CleanerCrm.Notifications.reminder_status_for_job/1` for that board to consume, following the same defensive-integration pattern its owner already used for schedule-change alerts (`latest_schedule_change_for_job/2`, which I also implemented since another agent's code already called it).

`mix compile`/`mix format` are clean, `mix test` is 146/146, and a full `mix spex` run shows no regressions in the previously-passing stories (832, 834) — the other 53 failures across the suite are pre-existing gaps in other stories still under construction by other agents (missing `FieldLive` routes, etc.), unrelated to this work.

I've sent a detailed handoff message to the team lead covering these results and the two known blockers.

        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "the office pushed a same-day schedule change to me 10 minutes ago", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        cleaner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), cleaner)
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            scheduled_date: Date.utc_today()
          })

        notification =
          Fixtures.schedule_change_notification_fixture(context.scope, cleaner, job, %{
            pushed_at: DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), -600, :second)
          })

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           cleaner: cleaner,
           cleaner_conn: cleaner_conn,
           job: job,
           notification: notification
         })}
      end

      given_ "I still have not acknowledged it", context do
        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the escalation window elapses", context do
        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the notification is re-sent to me via the fallback channel", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        assert has_element?(
                 board_live,
                 "[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-notification-channel']",
                 "SMS"
               )

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :board_live, board_live)}
      end

      then_ "the change is flagged to the office as unacknowledged and escalated", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.board_live,
                 "[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-ack-status']",
                 "Escalated"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story843.Criterion7203Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 843 — Get loud, acknowledged alerts when my schedule changes
  Criterion 7203 — Push failure falls back to SMS

  "My push notification cannot be delivered" is modeled as the cleaner
  having no push channel registered (`push_enabled: false`) — there is
  no push-registration flow anywhere in this app, so a cleaner who has
  never enabled push is the natural, real-world precondition rather
  than a fabricated delivery-status callback. "The system sends the
  change" re-drives the same real trigger as criterion 7190 (moving a
  job on `ScheduleLive.Board`); the fallback is observed via the
  board's per-job notification-channel control
  (`[data-test='job-<id>-notification-channel']`), never a live
  Twilio call.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a schedule change falls back to SMS when push cannot be delivered" do
    scenario "push failure falls back to SMS" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a schedule change needs to reach me", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
            push_enabled: false
          })

        cleaner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), cleaner)
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
            start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[14:30:00]
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, cleaner_conn: cleaner_conn, job: job})}
      end

      given_ "my push notification cannot be delivered", context do
        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the system sends the change", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        board_live
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-start-time-input']")
        |> render_change(%{"start_time" => "15:00"})

        {:ok, context}

      then_ "it falls back to sending me an SMS with the change details", context do

                 "SMS"

        assert has_element?(
                 board_live,
                 "[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-notification-channel']",
                 "3:00 PM"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.User do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  schema "users" do
    field :email, :string
    field :name, :string
    field :password, :string, virtual: true, redact: true
    field :hashed_password, :string, redact: true
    field :confirmed_at, :utc_datetime
    field :authenticated_at, :utc_datetime, virtual: true

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime)
  end

  @doc """
  A user changeset for registering or changing the email.

  It requires the email to change otherwise an error is added.

  ## Options

    * `:validate_unique` - Set to false if you don't want to validate the
      uniqueness of the email, useful when displaying live validations.
      Defaults to `true`.
  """
  def email_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
    user
    |> cast(attrs, [:email])
    |> validate_email(opts)
  end

  defp validate_email(changeset, opts) do
    changeset =
      changeset
      |> validate_required([:email])
      |> validate_format(:email, ~r/^[^@,;\s]+@[^@,;\s]+$/,
        message: "must have the @ sign and no spaces"
      )
      |> validate_length(:email, max: 160)

    if Keyword.get(opts, :validate_unique, true) do
      changeset
      |> unsafe_validate_unique(:email, CleanerCrm.Repo)
      |> unique_constraint(:email)
      |> validate_email_changed()
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  defp validate_email_changed(changeset) do
    if get_field(changeset, :email) && get_change(changeset, :email) == nil do
      add_error(changeset, :email, "did not change")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  @doc """
  A user changeset for changing the password.

  It is important to validate the length of the password, as long passwords may
  be very expensive to hash for certain algorithms.

  ## Options

    * `:hash_password` - Hashes the password so it can be stored securely
      in the database and ensures the password field is cleared to prevent
      leaks in the logs. If password hashing is not needed and clearing the
      password field is not desired (like when using this changeset for
      validations on a LiveView form), this option can be set to `false`.
      Defaults to `true`.
  """
  def password_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
    user
    |> cast(attrs, [:password])
    |> validate_confirmation(:password, message: "does not match password")
    |> validate_password(opts)
  end

  defp validate_password(changeset, opts) do
    changeset
    |> validate_required([:password])
    |> validate_length(:password, min: 12, max: 72)
    # Examples of additional password validation:
    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[a-z]/, message: "at least one lower case character")
    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[A-Z]/, message: "at least one upper case character")
    # |> validate_format(:password, ~r/[!?@#$%^&*_0-9]/, message: "at least one digit or punctuation character")
    |> maybe_hash_password(opts)
  end

  defp maybe_hash_password(changeset, opts) do
    hash_password? = Keyword.get(opts, :hash_password, true)
    password = get_change(changeset, :password)

    if hash_password? && password && changeset.valid? do
      changeset
      # If using Bcrypt, then further validate it is at most 72 bytes long
      |> validate_length(:password, max: 72, count: :bytes)
      # Hashing could be done with `Ecto.Changeset.prepare_changes/2`, but that
      # would keep the database transaction open longer and hurt performance.
      |> put_change(:hashed_password, Bcrypt.hash_pwd_salt(password))
      |> delete_change(:password)
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Confirms the account by setting `confirmed_at`.
  """
  def confirm_changeset(user) do
    now = DateTime.utc_now(:second)
    change(user, confirmed_at: now)
  end

  @doc """
  Verifies the password.

  If there is no user or the user doesn't have a password, we call
  `Bcrypt.no_user_verify/0` to avoid timing attacks.
  """
  def valid_password?(%CleanerCrm.Users.User{hashed_password: hashed_password}, password)
      when is_binary(hashed_password) and byte_size(password) > 0 do
    Bcrypt.verify_pass(password, hashed_password)
  end

  def valid_password?(_, _) do
    Bcrypt.no_user_verify()
    false
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
4	  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
5	  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
6	  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.
7	
8	  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
9	  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
10	  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
11	  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
12	  """
13	
14	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
15	
16	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
17	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
18	
19	  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{
20	    Notification,
21	    ReminderNotifier,
22	    ReminderScheduler,
23	    ReminderSettings
24	  }
25	
26	  ## Reminder settings
27	
28	  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
29	  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
30	    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
31	      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
32	      settings -> settings
33	    end
34	  end
35	
36	  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
37	    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
38	  end
39	
40	  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
41	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
42	    scope
43	    |> get_reminder_settings()
44	    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
45	    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
46	  end
47	
48	  @doc "Runs the periodic reminder scan now — see `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler`."
49	  defdelegate send_due_reminders(), to: ReminderScheduler, as: :scan_and_send
50	
51	  ## Notifications
52	
53	  def create_notification(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
54	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
55	    %Notification{account_id: account_id}
56	    |> Notification.changeset(attrs)
57	    |> Repo.insert()
58	  end
59	
60	  @doc "The office's delivery log: every notification for the account, most recent first."
61	  def list_notifications(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
62	    Notification
63	    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id)
64	    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
65	    |> preload([:client, :cleaner])
66	    |> Repo.all()
67	  end
68	
69	  ## Public confirm/reschedule — reached by token, no scope available
70	
71	  def get_notification_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
72	    Repo.get_by(Notification, token: token)
73	  end
74	
75	  def confirm_reminder(token) when is_binary(token) do
76	    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
77	      update_status(notification, status: :confirmed, confirmed_at: DateTime.utc_now())
78	    else
79	      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
80	    end
81	  end
82	
83	  def request_reschedule(token) when is_binary(token) do
84	    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
85	      update_status(notification,
86	        status: :reschedule_requested,
87	        reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.utc_now()
88	      )
89	    else
90	      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
91	    end
92	  end
93	
94	  @doc "True once the client has confirmed the most recent reminder sent for this job."
95	  def job_confirmed?(job_id) do
96	    Notification
97	    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :confirmed)
98	    |> Repo.exists?()
99	  end
100	
101	  @doc "True once the client has asked to reschedule via the most recent reminder for this job."
102	  def reschedule_requested?(job_id) do
103	    Notification
104	    |> where(
105	      [n],
106	      n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :reschedule_requested
107	    )
108	    |> Repo.exists?()
109	  end
110	
111	  @doc """
112	  The client's confirm/reschedule decision on their most recent
113	  reminder for this job, for `ScheduleLive.Index` to render on the
114	  board — `nil` (no decision yet), `:confirmed`, or
115	  `:reschedule_requested`.
116	  """
117	  def reminder_status_for_job(job_id) do
118	    Notification
119	    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder)
120	    |> where([n], n.status in [:confirmed, :reschedule_requested])
121	    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
  @moduledoc """
  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{
    Notification,
    ReminderNotifier,
    ReminderScheduler,
    ReminderSettings
  }

  ## Reminder settings

  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings
    end
  end

  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
  end

  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_reminder_settings()
    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  @doc "Runs the periodic reminder scan now — see `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler`."
  defdelegate send_due_reminders(), to: ReminderScheduler, as: :scan_and_send

  ## Notifications

  def create_notification(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Notification{account_id: account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "The office's delivery log: every notification for the account, most recent first."
  def list_notifications(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> preload([:client, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Public confirm/reschedule — reached by token, no scope available

  def get_notification_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Repo.get_by(Notification, token: token)
  end

  def confirm_reminder(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :confirmed, confirmed_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  def request_reschedule(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification,
        status: :reschedule_requested,
        reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.utc_now()
      )
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "True once the client has confirmed the most recent reminder sent for this job."
  def job_confirmed?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :confirmed)
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc "True once the client has asked to reschedule via the most recent reminder for this job."
  def reschedule_requested?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :reschedule_requested
    )
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc """
  The client's confirm/reschedule decision on their most recent
  reminder for this job, for `ScheduleLive.Index` to render on the
  board — `nil` (no decision yet), `:confirmed`, or
  `:reschedule_requested`.
  """
  def reminder_status_for_job(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder)
    |> where([n], n.status in [:confirmed, :reschedule_requested])
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> select([n], n.status)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  ## Twilio delivery-status webhook

  @doc """
  Applies a Twilio status callback: marks the matching notification
  delivered or undelivered, and — for an undeliverable SMS reminder —
  falls back to emailing the client and flags it for office visibility.
  """
  def handle_delivery_status(%{"MessageSid" => sid, "MessageStatus" => status} = params)
      when is_binary(sid) do
    case Repo.get_by(Notification, provider_message_id: sid) do
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      notification -> apply_delivery_status(notification, status, params["ErrorCode"])
    end
  end

  def handle_delivery_status(_params), do: {:error, :invalid_payload}

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, "delivered", _error_code) do
    update_status(notification, status: :delivered, delivered_at: DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, status, error_code)
       when status in ["failed", "undelivered"] do
    with {:ok, updated} <-
           update_status(notification, status: :undelivered, failure_reason: error_code || status) do
      maybe_fallback_to_email(updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, _status, _error_code), do: {:ok, notification}

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(
         %Notification{kind: :reminder, channel: :sms, client_id: client_id} = notification
       )
       when not is_nil(client_id) do
    client = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, notification.client_id)
    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, notification.job_id)
    token = generate_token()

    confirm_url = reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")
    reschedule_url = reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")

    {:ok, _email} = ReminderNotifier.deliver_reminder(client, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url)

    %Notification{account_id: notification.account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(%{
      client_id: client.id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :reminder,
      channel: :email,
      status: :sent,
      token: token,
      sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(_notification), do: :ok

  ## Schedule-change alerts (story 843 groundwork)

  def acknowledge(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :acknowledged, acknowledged_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "Pending schedule-change alerts a cleaner hasn't acknowledged yet, for office visibility."
  def list_unacknowledged(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.kind == :schedule_change and n.status == :pending
    )
    |> preload([:cleaner, :job])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  The most recent schedule-change alert pushed for this job — `nil`,
  or a `Notification` exposing `:status`
  (`:pending` | `:acknowledged` | `:escalated`) and `:channel`
  (`:push` | `:sms` | `:email`). This is the contract
  `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Index` reads defensively to show a job's
  ack status on the board.
  """
  def latest_schedule_change_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, job_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :schedule_change
    )
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  ## Shared helpers

  @doc false
  def generate_token, do: Base.url_encode64(:crypto.strong_rand_bytes(24), padding: false)

  defp update_status(%Notification{} = notification, attrs) do
    notification
    |> Notification.changeset(Map.new(attrs))
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp reminder_url(path), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> path
end
